discovery: Fluctuation theorems and nonequilibrium work relations for small systems

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

subfield: Nonequilibrium statistical physics / stochastic and quantum thermodynamics
motivation: Evans and coworkers (1993) discovered the fluctuation theorem: entropy production far from equilibrium obeys an exact symmetry, so violations of the second law in small systems occur with precisely quantifiable probabilities. Jarzynski (1997) showed that equilibrium free-energy differences follow exactly from work done in arbitrarily fast, irreversible processes. Crooks (1999) unified both in a detailed fluctuation relation for work distributions. These are rare exact statements valid arbitrarily far from equilibrium and across platforms. They have been confirmed in single-molecule pulling, colloidal traps, single-electron boxes and trapped ions. They are now standard tools for measuring free energies in biophysics. They also underpin stochastic and quantum thermodynamics, including thermodynamic uncertainty relations, fluctuation-dissipation bounds and limits on the precision and efficiency of nanoscale engines and quantum devices. Together they changed how physicists understand the second law at the nanoscale.
